title: Build now, grow later

readouts.v: Output above normal capacity: overtime and stretched firms push prices up.

predict.q: Start: the economy is producing **1,000** at full capacity; price level **100**. The government spends **50** a year on roads and broadband. In the **short run**, while the building goes on, what happens?

options.s: Output and the price level both rise
options.fb: While building goes on, spending rises at once: output 1,050 and price level 105, with firms stretched above normal capacity.

options.s: Capacity jumps at once, so the price level falls
options.fb: The new capacity is not there yet. The spending comes first.

options.s: Nothing happens until the roads and broadband are finished
options.fb: Builders are paid while the work goes on, so spending rises straight away.

options.s: Output rises but the price level stays at 100
options.fb: When firms are already at full capacity, extra spending pushes prices up too.

task: Move the **spending** slider; then switch the **time** control from "short run" to "long run".

target.do: Set spending to 50 (short run), then press Check.

takeaway: Short run (extra spending) output **1,050**, price level **105**; long run, once capacity grows, output **1,100** and the price level back to **100**.
